findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The only certified food protection manager was not present during the visit. There wasn't any cooking occurring, however, the facility was in the process of butchering meats on site. Any time food handling, cooking, or preparation is occurring, a CFPM is needed. Ensure that there is at least two employees who are food manager certified to cover all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Baked potatoes stored in the heat and serve cooler (floor cooler) were observed without date marking. There should be either a sell by date or preparation date indicated on the packaging of the food. The items should be held for no longer than 7 days of preparation. A label was created with the correct use-by-date. Ensure that cooked and cooled items served for grab-and-go service are date marked and never held for longer than 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: A gallon of unopened whole milk stored in the walk in cooler was observed to exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date (2/24/2025). Discussed and shown to the PIC and the gallon of milk was discarded. Ensure that milks stored in house never exceed the manufacturer's use-by-date.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-304.15: inspector observed the employee go from food prep to the walk in cooler and back to food prep with no glove change. Gloves were changed and hands were washed. Ensure that gloves are changed and hands are washed any time there is an interruption in operation. 

(A) If used, SINGLE-USE gloves shall be used for only one task such as working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD or with raw animal FOOD, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
3-602.11: Inspector observed grab and go items to not include complete labels. Provide labels according the code requirements.

(A) FOOD PACKAGED in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be properly labeled. (B) Regulatory requirements-(1) The common name of the FOOD/identity statement; 106 (2) List ingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, declaration of artificial colors and flavors and chemical preservatives; (3) net contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (5) MAJOR FOOD ALLERGENS. Pf (6) Nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling UNLESS EXEMPT Under FDCA. (Pf) (C) Bulk FOOD for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be labeled in plain view. (D) Bulk, unPACKAGED FOODS portioned for CONSUMERS shall be properly labeled.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observe employee to make sani bucket utilizing the hand sink. Hand sink’s are for handwashing ONLY. Cease practice. Discussed with employee. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed fans on ceiling of the meat prep area in back to have dust accumulation. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 5/13/21 and 9/13/21.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed pizza chest freezer (“Blue Bunny” freezer) to have a large accumulation of frost. Ensure routine de-frosting of freezer in order to hinder frost build-up.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the following NonFOOD-contact areas to have dust and debris:
1. Fans on ceiling of the meat prep area in back have dust accumulation. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 5/13/21.
2. Dust on fans inside reach-in cooler near the big double doors/by water fountains. 
3. Fan on floor of the customer meat display counter area has accumulation of dust.

Ensure routine cleaning of NonFOOD-contact surfaces.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed fans in walk-in cooler and fans in meat prep area in back to have large accumulation of dust. Ensure routine cleaning to avoid dust accumulation on fans.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed both the back deli meat prep area hand sink and 3 compartment sink in this area to have caulk missing between sinks and wall. Discussed caulking with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/29/20.

Observed both men and women's bathrooms to have caulk coming away from hand sink and wall. Discussed re-caulking with PIC.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed no food handler's licenses in public health folder. Discussed keeping copies of food handler's licenses with the certified food manager licenses in the folder. Ensure copies are kept at facility.
